3481597.title: The Painters
3481597.overview: The Painters is a non-verbal performance built on an unusual combination: dance, comedy, and live art-making on stage. Projection mapping adds a layer of moving imagery over the painting itself, so every scene doubles as a visual show. Signature acts include light carving (sculpting images out of light), four-panel action painting, dust drawing with its trademark reveal, high-speed drawing, marbling painted on water, and glow-in-the-dark drawing. Because the show has no dialogue, it works equally well for visitors who speak no Korean.
3481597.fee: VIP 70,000 won · R 60,000 won · S 50,000 won
3481597.hours: 14:00 / 17:00 / 20:00 · Schedule may change depending on the producer

292961.title: Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony at Deoksugung Palace
292961.overview: The Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony is Seoul's flagship historical reenactment: the changing of the sumungun, the guards who kept the gates of Joseon-era palaces. Reconstructed from historical records, the ceremony unfolds in front of Daehanmun Gate at Deoksugung Palace, six days a week (closed Mondays) at 11:00 and 14:00. Hands-on programs run alongside it — beat the drum that opens the ceremony, dress as a gate guard yourself, or put on Joseon-era costume for photos. It is free, central, and one of the easiest ways to see living Joseon court ritual in the middle of modern Seoul.
292961.place: In front of Daehanmun Gate, Deoksugung Palace

2809535.title: Namsan Beacon Ceremony and Traditional Culture Events
2809535.overview: In the Joseon era, the beacon mound on Namsan was the final relay point of a nationwide signal-fire network that carried news to the capital. This Seoul city program brings that system back to life: watch the beacon-lighting ceremony with historical commentary at the Namsan beacon site, join the daily noon bell-ringing at Bosingak Pavilion, and catch samulnori percussion and traditional martial-arts demonstrations at the Palgakjeong plaza by N Seoul Tower. Day programs let visitors try the night-watch and beacon-keeper roles themselves.
2809535.place: Namsan Beacon Mound and Bosingak Pavilion

3473295.title: DDP Architecture Tour
3473295.overview: A guided walk through Dongdaemun Design Plaza, the landmark designed by Zaha Hadid, covering both the building itself and the history of the Dongdaemun area it sits in. Tours run Tuesday through Sunday (closed Mondays and on New Year's Day, Seollal, and Chuseok). The English tour departs at 13:30; Korean tours run at 10:30 and 15:30. Meet at the tour desk on the first floor of the DDP Museum; the walk takes about 60 minutes. Ages 13 and up; children under 13 must be accompanied by a guardian. Book online via the DDP website, or take a remaining spot on site from 10 minutes before departure.
3473295.fee: Adults 10,000 won · Veterans, military, visitors with disabilities, youth groups 8,000 won · Children 5,000 won

3107059.title: Sungnyemun Gate Guard Ceremony 2026
3107059.overview: Pasu — standing guard over the capital's walls — was one of the key military rituals of the Joseon dynasty, and this reenactment restores it at Sungnyemun, Korea's National Treasure gate. Guards line up before the gate, the timekeeper announces the hour, conch and trumpet signals sound, and the gate-opening ritual begins on the commander's order, followed by six rounds of guard duty and shift changes before the closing ritual. Runs daily except Mondays, 10:00–15:40, free of charge — an easy add-on to any walk between Seoul Station and Myeong-dong.

2433596.title: Walk of the Royal Family
2433596.overview: A palace procession inside an airport: before your flight out of Incheon International, you can watch a reenactment of Joseon court life. In Terminal 1, the king and queen stroll the concourse as if walking the palace grounds; in Terminal 2, a royal procession with military officials recreates a late-Joseon martial exam visit. After each performance, visitors can take photos with the cast in full court dress. A rare chance to see Joseon pageantry without leaving the departures hall.

4067214.title: 2026 Visit Korean Islands Year
4067214.overview: 2026 is Korea's official Year of Island Tourism, a national campaign spotlighting the ecology and culture of the country's thousands of islands. It ties into the 2026 Yeosu World Island Exhibition — the first world expo dedicated to islands — and spreads the momentum nationwide with island travel subsidies, culture weeks, and events running throughout the year. If island-hopping in the South Sea archipelago is on your list, 2026 is the year the infrastructure, discounts, and programming all line up.
4067214.sponsor: Ministry of the Interior and Safety

3488655.title: 2026 Culture Day: Cheongchun Mic (Jeolla & Jeju)
3488655.overview: Cheongchun Mic is a national busking program that puts young and senior performing teams on outdoor stages across the Jeolla and Jeju regions, part of Korea's monthly Culture Day initiative. The 2026 edition pairs emerging local acts with everyday public spaces — parks, plazas, street corners — so residents and travelers run into live performance as part of daily life. Around 47 performances are scheduled; times vary by show.
3488655.place: Gwangju Jungoe Park and venues across Jeolla and Jeju
3488655.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

3492276.title: 2026 Culture Day: Cheongchun Mic (Seoul, Gyeonggi & Gangwon)
3492276.overview: The capital-region and Gangwon leg of Cheongchun Mic, Korea's Culture Day street-performance program. Young and senior performing teams selected by open call take their acts to streets and plazas across Seoul, Gyeonggi, and Gangwon from April through November. Expect anything from acoustic sets to dance crews — free, outdoors, and deliberately placed where people already are.
3492276.place: Across the capital region and Gangwon
3492276.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

3377038.title: 2026 International Seon Meditation Conference
3377038.overview: Hosted by the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism, this conference-and-festival pairing explores Seon (Zen) meditation as a tool for mental health, now in its third year. The 2026 theme is 'Seon Meditation in the Age of AI'. Alongside the conference sessions, a public meditation festival at Bongeunsa Temple lets visitors try various forms of Seon practice first-hand — in one of the few major temples standing directly across from Gangnam's COEX skyline.
3377038.place: Bongeunsa Temple and Bongeun Culture Center

2987489.title: Goheung Nokdong Port Drone Show 2026
2987489.overview: A recurring night-sky drone show over Nokdong Port in Goheung, one of the darker, clearer coastal skies in Jeollanam-do. Regular shows run Saturdays at 21:00 at the Nokdong Port sea garden, with a larger 900-drone show in front of the county office plaza on the last Friday of each month (April–October), preceded by an open-air busking stage at 20:00. Holiday specials are added around New Year sunrise and Seollal. Shows may move or cancel in bad weather.
2987489.hours: Sat 21:00 (Nokdong Port) · Last Fri of the month 21:00 (county plaza)

3478890.title: Geumnam-ro Car-Free Street 'Geotjaing' 2026
3478890.overview: On the first Saturday of each month from April to November, Gwangju closes Geumnam-ro — the city's most symbolic downtown boulevard — to cars. The name Geotjaing blends the local dialect for 'let's walk' with '-ing'. The street fills with walkers, pop-up culture programs, and performances, part of the city's push toward transit, cycling, and walking. A good date to aim for if you want to see downtown Gwangju at its liveliest.
3478890.hours: 13:00–19:00 · First Saturday of the month, Apr–Nov

2865136.title: Chungjang Raon Festa 2026
2865136.overview: A monthly street festival in Gwangju's Chungjang-ro shopping district, running the first Saturday of each month from April. Launched in 2022 to revive the downtown commercial area, it layers culture and hands-on programs over the streets and underground arcade — music, markets, and family-friendly events. Times vary by program; the district itself is Gwangju's classic downtown, dense with shops and street food.
2865136.hours: Varies by program · First Saturday of the month
2865136.sponsor: Dong-gu, Gwangju · Chungjang District Revitalization Team

3512205.title: Seogwipo Old Downtown Culture Festival 2026
3512205.overview: Evening performances on Ijungseop-ro, the artist street in Seogwipo's old downtown on Jeju Island. Under festival lighting, the street hosts music, dance, and performance acts every Friday through Sunday at 19:00, from April 11 to October 30. It pairs naturally with the Lee Jung-seop gallery and the street market nearby — come for dinner, stay for the show. Performances may be cancelled in bad weather, so check ahead.

4058556.title: Culture Lounge Gyeonggi-Jang
4058556.overview: A hands-on cultural space in Suwon showcasing local content from across Gyeonggi Province in one place. 'Local Radar' builds a personalized Gyeonggi travel plan around your tastes; the 'Gyeonggi Ceramics Shop' combines pottery-craft experiences with tea tasting. The space mixes exhibition, performance, and participation — less a museum than a browsing room for what the province around Seoul has to offer.

3111722.title: Hangang River History Tour
3111722.overview: Guided walking tours along the Han River, pairing riverside scenery with the history layered around it. Sixteen courses cover different stretches of the river and nearby heritage sites, each led by a Hangang interpreter. Tours run in two daily slots (10:00–12:00 and 14:00–16:00) and take about two hours. It is one of the simplest ways to turn a riverside walk into something with a storyline — though note the commentary is primarily in Korean.
3111722.place: Hangang parks and nearby heritage sites

2766000.title: NAORA Show: Night of Light
2766000.overview: A night media-art show at Ganhyeon Tourist Area in Wonju, where sheer rock cliffs meet a slow river. Part one is a warm-up of busking, live instruments, and dance; the finale projects video across a natural rock face 250m wide and 70m tall using 12 projectors and 7 lasers, synchronized with a musical fountain that fires jets up to 60m high. It shares the site with the Sogeumsan Grand Valley suspension bridges — do the skywalk before dark, then stay for the show.
2766000.place: NAORA Show Plaza, Sogeumsan Grand Valley

2434545.title: Saeyeongyo Bridge Weekend Show
2434545.overview: Seogwipo's signature night program at Saeyeongyo Bridge, where performances meet the harbor scenery. Every Friday and Saturday evening from late April through October, the waterfront hosts music, dance, and performance acts under the lights, capped by a fireworks show over the water and a musical fountain. Afterward, cross the bridge for a lit-up night walk on Saeseom Island. Schedules can shift with the weather.

4062805.title: Goesan Space City: Star Explorers
4062805.overview: A hands-on children's exhibition at the Goesan Eco Museum built around an imagined 'space ecology', exploring fruits and plants through seeing, touching, and moving. Kids question, imagine, and build their own stories through the interactive course, with parents cast as fellow guides on the expedition. A useful rainy-day or family stop if you are in the Chungbuk countryside.

2720203.title: Seoul Street Performance: Every Corner Live 2026
2720203.overview: 150 artist teams selected by open call perform across central Seoul's streets and plazas through late November. The point is the surprise: performances appear where people already are — station exits, plazas, park corners — rather than on ticketed stages. Free by nature; times and spots vary by performance.

3116066.title: Hangang Night View Tour
3116066.overview: A relaxed guided night walk along the Han River with stories behind the skyline, on two courses: the Banpo Moonlight Course (Seorae Island, Some Sevit, the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain, and Jamsugyo Bridge) and the Yeouido Starlight Course (Hangang Art Park, Mapo Bridge, the floating stage, and the water-light plaza). Runs Friday and Saturday evenings, 19:00–20:30. Free, but spots are allocated by lottery.

2657619.title: Hwaseong Haenggung Palace Night Opening 2026
2657619.overview: Hwaseong Haenggung — the grandest of Korea's temporary royal palaces, built for King Jeongjo's visits to Suwon — opens after dark for its signature night program, 'Moonlight Hwadam: Stories of Flowers under the Moon'. Flower installations and atmospheric lighting turn the palace courtyards into a slow evening walk, quieter and more intimate than daytime visits. It sits inside the UNESCO-listed Hwaseong Fortress, so you can pair it with a night walk on the fortress wall.
2657619.fee: Adults 2,000 won · Youth/military 1,500 won · Children 1,000 won

2598331.title: Culture Flows at Seoul Plaza
2598331.overview: Free open-air concerts on the outdoor stage at Seoul Plaza, running roughly eight months from May to December. The 2026 season opens on May 6 and cycles through pop, hip-hop, jazz, bands, and performance acts month by month, in the plaza in front of City Hall — easy to fold into any evening downtown.

2774275.title: Mokpo Marine W Show 2026
2774275.overview: Mokpo's flagship night show and one of the signature attractions of this southern port city: a multimedia performance combining a floating sea stage, Korea's largest marine fountain, and fireworks over the water. Over five years it has drawn more than a million viewers across 51 shows. The 2026 edition scales up the sea-stage performances, fireworks, and choreographed fountain work. Free viewing from Peace Plaza on the waterfront.

4082595.title: Palsaek Chanran: Regions Full of K
4082595.overview: A special exhibition at the Cheong Wa Dae Sarangchae asking where the 'K' in K-culture actually comes from. Through regional-content displays and media art, it traces how local histories, arts, and cultural assets across Korea's provinces feed into today's K-content — an argument that hallyu's roots run through the regions, not just Seoul. Runs through December on the first floor of Sarangchae, next to the former presidential compound.
4082595.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

3495437.title: 2026 Culture Day: Culture Delivery
3495437.overview: A traveling arts program that brings street performances to places with the least access to culture — remote villages, border areas, and industrial districts across the capital region and Gangwon. Young and senior performing teams stage free shows in everyday local spaces from June to October, delivering the arts to audiences who rarely get them nearby.
3495437.place: Samgot-ri Village, Yeoncheon and other sites
3495437.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism

4102351.title: Masterpieces and Teatime: A Cup of Calm in Light and Color
4102351.overview: A themed exhibition at the Andamiro Gwittae Museum pairing famous paintings of tea with the real teapots and cups depicted in them. When the Age of Exploration carried tea from Asia to Europe, it carried the vessels too — and painters began capturing the warmth of teatime in luminous color. From the quiet glow of William McGregor Paxton's 'Tea Leaves' to the silver teapot in Mary Cassatt's 'The Tea', the show lets you stand in front of the scene and the object at once.

4094595.title: Contemporary Artist Project: Lee Wan — I Write
4094595.overview: An exhibition at the Seoul Arts Center's Calligraphy Museum reinterpreting traditional Korean calligraphy through contemporary art. Working from brush and ink, artist Lee Wan combines script, image, painting, and seal-carving to push at what calligraphy can be — and asks not 'is the writing beautiful' but 'why do we write at all'. A compact, thoughtful show where tradition and contemporary practice meet.
4094595.place: Gallery 3, Calligraphy Museum, Seoul Arts Center
4094595.fee: Adults 5,000 won · Ages 3–19 2,500 won · Seniors 65+ 3,000 won · Free for visitors with disabilities, veterans, Art Pass holders

606549.title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival
606549.overview: Korea's leading photography festival, held since 2002 in Yeongwol, a mountain county in Gangwon-do. The 24th edition runs July 17 to October 11 across the DongGang Museum of Photography and venues around the county. Highlights include the DongGang Photography Award exhibition — this year featuring Im An-na — and an open-call international show of 19 photographers selected from worldwide submissions, alongside a full slate of themed exhibitions. Worth combining with Yeongwol's river valleys and the Jangneung royal tomb.
606549.fee: Adults 3,000 won · Youth/military 2,000 won · Children 1,000 won
606549.sponsor: DongGang Photo Village Committee · Yeongwol Foundation for Culture and Tourism

4102649.title: Texture of Rest
4102649.overview: The Wooran Foundation's second textile exhibition offers fiber art as an answer to modern overload. Taking textiles' inherent qualities — connection and patience — as its medium, the show frames weaving as a way of re-threading a scattered self: not avoiding difficulty but passing through it toward genuine rest. A quiet, meditative stop in Seongsu-dong, Seoul's converted-warehouse art district.
